title: Tech & architecture slides for the Elisa deck
subtitle: Two slides for deck-writer: the architecture slide replaces the tier table on the solution slide, the gates slide goes right after it
footer: Recordly | Elisa | Data platform architecture and tool selection

slides.title: Real-time where a domain needs it, on your own Google Cloud stack. Literal zero-batch is not achievable for reconciled finance
bullets: **Freshness per domain, not one rule:** each domain gets the slowest tier that still meets its tested need. Target ranges per tier are agreed at Gate 1, after we measure current freshness.

**Why not literally everything real-time:** finance close reconciles daily, and streaming all data raises run cost, failure surface and the retention exposure of traffic data. Option C, all real-time as written, is scored with its cost so the committee decides.

**Existing services first:** Pub/Sub and change capture are proposed Google Cloud options, not assumed to be in your stack today. No new licence, no AI or ML, no new platform unless a tested need fails.

slides.title: Technical gates: nothing is locked before it is measured
table: NDA and secrecy undertaking signed; read-only Elisa-issued roles on BigQuery, Composer and Looker metadata and logs; no subscriber rows leave your GCP project; plus a write-enabled sandbox dataset and one feed, in your project, for the latency test (synthetic or masked data only)

Each priority domain (3 to 5, chosen with you by sprint day 2, the rest listed as out of scope) has an owner, a stated freshness need and current freshness measured from logs; one real feed run Pub/Sub to BigQuery to Looker in a sandbox dataset, latency measured from event to a Looker tile with the cache setting stated; freshness defined as event time to visible in Looker, reported as median and 95th percentile, per tier; ERP named with its change-capture options; target range per tier agreed

Options A tuned, B tiered, C all real-time scored on latency, cost and quota per tier, Composer load, failure mode and effort; every score cites a measurement or is marked 'not tested'; same IAM and policy-tag behaviour tested in Looker and Power BI on the tested domain; if the measured 95th percentile misses the Gate 1 range, the tier is re-scoped or Option C is costed for that domain, and the miss is shown to the committee
Target architecture and roadmap accepted by the steering committee; plan for existing Composer pipelines: keep, change or retire, per DAG group; anything untested marked 'not tested'
slides.note: Unknowns and how each is settled: which ERP and its change capture (sprint; without change capture the ERP domain runs API polling or micro-batch, and Gate 1 shows its measured delay against the stated need) · Power BI connectivity (import refreshes on a schedule; DirectQuery is not a seconds path, its freshness is bounded by query load, limits and cost; measured per report in the sprint) · sandbox dataset and feed (requested before day 1; if none by day 3, the latency test is marked 'not tested' and streaming stays a proposal) · real freshness need per domain (owners answer in your chat tool by week 2) · where Composer code, CI/CD and access policies live (recorded in the sprint; existing pipelines stay unless a test fails).
